analysis:
The PR adds an add-on hold feature: a local AF_UNIX socket (~/.darkbloom/runtime/addon.sock), an operator mailbox, persisted holds with 30-600 s leases, an ownership.lock probe, and optional busy_reason/busy_since_ms/busy_addon fields on register and heartbeat. The rest is documentation plus the threat-model additions A-018, TB-012 and T-059.

No concrete regression was found in the supplied evidence. I discarded the prior unit-23 finding that the add-on IPC is not covered by the threat model, because this PR itself adds TB-012, T-059 and A-018 in docs/threat-model.yaml. The earlier concerns that the TB-012 reference was dangling are resolved by the same additions. The finding's claim about fail-open on an unreadable hold record is a documented behavior (addon-hold.md failure modes) and is same-UID scoped, so it does not qualify as a regression.

Verified from the supplied source:
- AddonPeerPolicy (per-request LOCAL_PEERTOKEN, same euid, Developer ID requirement, hardened runtime, DEBUG-only dev identity).
- AddonIPCServer (0700 directory, 0600 socket, 8 KiB cap, 8 connections, timeouts).
- AddonHoldStore (O_NOFOLLOW, owner and mode checks, size cap, atomic write).
- The machine lock fails closed.
- handleAddonIPC binds the claimed add-on name to the verified signer.
- The hold keeps admission closed through reconnect, does not send provider_drain, and does not stop the App Attest worker. The worker-resume guards now use refusingForServiceChange.
- The busy fields are advisory and sent only beside draining. They cannot grant serving authorization, so T-053, T-052 and TB-011 are unaffected.
- The T-041 cache controls and the weight-hash gating are unchanged. Skipping persistLoadedModelSet during a hold is availability-neutral.

Residual items, none of which is a demonstrated defect:
- ProviderDrain internals (refusingForServiceChange, .addonHold takeover and resume) were not supplied.
- Handlers for load_model, prefetch and the local endpoint under a hold were not shown. The docs claim they are refused or deferred.
- The ProviderBusy encode/decode bounds on busy_addon and its coordinator-side sanitization are unverified, and coordinator handling is declared separate platform work.
- The DaemonState addonHold snapshot contents and state-file permissions were not visible.
- Same-UID abuse of the socket or the lock to hold the provider is accepted in T-059.
- Many integration-source units were omitted (241 of 490), so deeper review of the Addon/* sources is warranted.
